title: A Twin That Decides, a Model That Sleeps, and a 5G World Split in Two
text:
Networks · 5G & 6G
    
      
      
        
          arXiv
          PRISM: turning 6G digital twins from passive mirrors into reasoning systems
        
        
          PRISM reframes what a network digital twin is for. Today's twin-assisted ISAC frameworks sense continuously and indiscriminately, optimize a single task, and leave little room for persistent, multi-domain knowledge. PRISM makes the twin a persistent, network-wide reasoning engine that proactively directs sensing toward anticipated decision needs — sensing only what the next decision actually requires, rather than following a fixed schedule.In an XL-MIMO deployment mixing eMBB, URLLC, and mMTC, the decision-centric approach substantially cuts sensing overhead while preserving decision reliability and latency, and it supports slice-aware operation. The pitch is 6G self-awareness: the twin stops being a passive mirror and becomes the component that decides what to look at next.
          
          flowchart LR
  S[Sense the world] --> P[Predict outcomes]
  P --> D[What does the next decision need?]
  D --> T[Direct sensing to the gap]
  T --> S

          
        
        
          Why read it The cleanest recent statement of a twin as a decision engine rather than a mirror. If you care about where digital twins earn their keep in a network, the decision-centric sensing control is the mechanism to watch.
        
      
      
      
        
          arXiv
          Real-time OFDM radar inside an OpenAirInterface 5G base station with O-RAN sensing
        
        
          A real-time OFDM radar embedded directly in the OpenAirInterface 5G base-station process: it strips communication symbols by regularized element-wise division and runs range–Doppler processing plus ordered-statistic constant-false-alarm detection online, without modifying the 5G waveform. Nominal resolution is 2.57 m range and 0.28 m/s velocity, running live with a commercial UE on the same carrier and no measurable change to downlink throughput.The engineering is honest and the numbers specific: a carrier-dependent transmit–receive phase rotation on the USRP X300 was found and mitigated — a tuning-grid-aligned carrier improved mean-removal clutter suppression from −16.4 dB to 38.0 dB — and a custom E2SM-RADAR service exports detections to a near-real-time RAN Intelligent Controller for tracking, micro-Doppler analysis, and classification. This is integrated sensing and communication made real on open-source 5G.
          
        
        
          Why read it Concrete evidence that ISAC can share spectrum with live comms on an open 5G stack. If you audit or build on OAI, the E2SM-RADAR control-loop detail is directly reusable.
        
      
      
      
        
          Light Reading
          Nokia quits its China R&D hub as the 5G world splits into rival supply chains
        
        
          Nokia will close its Hangzhou radio R&D centre by the end of 2026, cutting around 1,600 jobs, less than a year after taking full control of Nokia Shanghai Bell. Greater China revenue has collapsed from about €2.2B in 2018 to €913M in 2025 — a 58% drop — while headcount fell from 13,700 to 7,200. The retreat tracks geopolitical retaliation after Sweden barred Chinese vendors.Read it as a supply-chain marker, not just a layoff: the world's 5G is visibly hardening into Western and Chinese stacks, with Huawei now roughly 59% of Germany's 5G network while Nokia holds under 3% in China. Nokia is re-pointing its R&D at 5G, optical, and data-center connectivity where it still expects growth.
          
        
        
          Why read it A durable structural signal for anyone tracking where 5G core/RAN intellectual property and supply chains actually live. The Western-versus-Chinese stack split is now a balance-sheet fact, not a talking point.
        
      
      
    
  



  
    Security
    
      
      
        
          arXiv
          Model hypnosis: additive, subliminal cues that steer LLMs
        
        
          Researchers show that individually weak, seemingly irrelevant prompt cues — paraphrases, typos, innocuous phrasing — can be systematically combined to strongly control model behavior, a phenomenon they call model hypnosis. It works across model families and scales, including frontier reasoning models, and hypnotic prompts transfer between models.Because control rides on inconspicuous textual choices, it is hard to spot or defend against, and it complicates interpretability: the model is being steered without any obvious command. The paper frames it as a major new surface for AI safety and a hurdle for anyone trying to explain why a model decided what it did.
          
        
        
          Why read it If you ship LLM systems where prompt-level control matters — moderation, agents, tooling — this is a threat model to plan around. Weak cues combining into strong control is exactly the kind of subtle failure that slips past red-teaming.
        
      
      
      
        
          arXiv
          A short study of exposed Starlink hosts: outdated OSes and weak protocols
        
        
          A measurement-driven look at the security of Starlink-connected hosts finds they are more likely to run outdated or vulnerable operating systems and network protocols than non-Starlink hosts. The risk skews hard by region — Latin America, Southeast Asia, and Eastern Europe show disproportionately higher exposure.The paper is short and deliberately scoped, an IMC workshop item, but the finding matters as satellite broadband moves from edge novelty to mainstream access: the user base is less mature, and there is no carrier-grade patching discipline behind it.
          
        
        
          Why read it A reminder that the attack surface of the next billion connected is immature. If you build or operate on LEO or satellite access, the regional risk skew is worth factoring into your threat model.
        
      
      
    
  



  
    AI & Models
    
      
      
        
          OpenRouter
          GPT-5.6 Sol's price just got cut in half on OpenRouter
        
        
          OpenRouter now lists GPT-5.6 Sol at half its previous price: input dropped from $5.00 to $2.50 per million tokens and output from $30.00 to $15.00, with cached input at $0.50. The weighted average customers actually pay sits even lower — roughly $0.90/M input and $20.46/M output across providers.It is a pricing signal, not a model release: frontier reasoning is getting cheaper at the API layer, which shifts the cost calculus for anyone weighing hosted frontier models against running open weights locally. The same page shows Sol holding up on GPQA Diamond (94.1%) and Terminal-Bench Hard (65.9%).
          
        
        
          Why read it A concrete data point for the hosted-versus-local cost decision. When the frontier price halves, the envelope for just use open-weights locally narrows — worth re-running your own cost model.
        
      
      
      
        
          GitHub
          llama.cpp hits v0.1.0 — the local-inference runtime finally gets a version number
        
        
          The workhorse of local inference moved from sequential build numbers to semantic versioning with its first tag: v0.1.0, cut August 17. It is a marker of maturity for the de facto standard runtime behind most on-device and edge LLM setups.The change is organizational more than functional, but it matters for anyone pinning builds in production: semantic versioning gives a cleaner upgrade path and a stable vocabulary for what changed between releases, instead of guessing from build-number deltas.
          
        
        
          Why read it If you run local or edge inference, the runtime you depend on just committed to a versioning contract. A good moment to standardize your own pinning strategy.
        
      
      
      
        
          arXiv
          Intern-S2-Mobius: a foundation model that separates knowledge from reasoning
        
        
          Mobius separates a globally shared memory — an FFN that stores knowledge vectors — from multiple reasoners, self-attention modules that iteratively pull the knowledge they need and do the composing. Knowledge and reasoning are decoupled, with hidden states acting as cache and carrier between the two.The payoff is efficiency: a 7B model trained from scratch matches a 7B transformer baseline with 62.6% of its training data, and Intern-S2-Mobius — continually pretrained from Qwen3.5-35B — delivers similar downstream scores with nearly 4× end-to-end inference speedup. For local inference, architectures that separate what it knows from how it thinks are a lever on both memory and speed.
          
          flowchart LR
  Q[Query] --> R[Reasoner<br/>self-attention]
  R -->|hidden state| M[Memory<br/>FFN knowledge store]
  M -->|knowledge vector| R
  R --> O[Answer]

          
        
        
          Why read it An architecture trend worth tracking: decoupling knowledge from reasoning trades parameter count for inference efficiency. If you evaluate open-weight models for local deployment, this is the kind of design that changes the speed-versus-size tradeoff.
        
      
      
      
        
          arXiv
          AlphaEvolve tightens the matrix-multiplication exponent to 2.371177
        
        
          DeepMind researchers improved the best-known bound on ω, the matrix-multiplication exponent, to 2.371177 — down from 2.371339 — by reformulating the core optimization problem of combination-loss analysis and then refining the solver with AlphaEvolve, the evolutionary optimizer behind recent AlphaTensor-style results.The gain is a hair on paper, but the process is the point: a machine-discovered optimization method tightening one of theoretical computer science's oldest open constants. ω feeds directly into the asymptotic cost of matrix multiply, the primitive at the bottom of nearly every ML workload.
          
        
        
          Why read it A small constant with a big shadow: each nudge to ω ripples through the theoretical cost of the linear algebra at the heart of ML. Worth a skim even if you never touch the proof.
        
      
      
    
  



  
    Research & World Models
    
      
      
        
          arXiv
          CaliBench: are video world models actually calibrated to physics?
        
        
          Video world models generate plausible-looking futures, but are the probabilities right? CaliBench scores them in physically interpretable spaces — a bin index, a die face, a suit, a colour — where the reference distribution is known in closed form, and decomposes performance into scorability (how often a scoreable outcome is produced) and calibration (total-variation distance from the reference).Across nine scenes and six image-to-video models (WAN-2.7, SeeDance-2.0, HappyHorse-1.0, Veo 3.1, Runway Gen-4.5, Cosmos3-Super), models consistently concentrate probability mass on a few outcomes rather than reproducing the reference — in the extreme, Veo 3.1 collapses to a single die face. Most scene–model pairs are significantly miscalibrated, and no model dominates all scenes.
          
        
        
          Why read it A reminder that looks right is not is right for world models. If you generate synthetic futures for planning or simulation, calibration — not just visual fidelity — is the property that makes them trustworthy.

title: A $7B Gateway, a Network That Knows You, and Machines That Dream
text:
Networks · 5G & 6G
    
      
      
        
          NTT DOCOMO
          NTT DOCOMO & Samsung validate user-level AI-RAN optimization
        
        
        
          AI-RANuser-levelnetwork intelligence
        
        
        
          Docomo and Samsung validated AI-RAN optimization that works at the individual-user level instead of applying one configuration per cell. The system learns each subscriber's movement and usage patterns, predicts service degradation before it happens, and adjusts network settings proactively. In simulations based on Docomo's commercial network data and a local 5G field trial in Japan (January 2026), the frequency of communication-speed degradation fell from 13.1% to 7.2% — roughly halved.The framing is explicitly 6G: an era where networks autonomously recognize user context and service requirements. The interesting engineering shift is the granularity — the difference between this cell is congested and this user's session is about to degrade implies a per-subscriber state model living in the RAN, with prediction running ahead of the congestion.
          
        
        
          Why read it A concrete data point for the predictive-network thesis. Cell-level vs user-level optimization is exactly where the network-intelligence story stops being a slide and starts being a system.
        
      
      
      
        
          Cenerva
          5G News Round-Up for the Week to 17 August 2026
        
        
        
          The week in 5G, condensed: T-Mobile completed the sale of its nationwide 800 MHz portfolio to Grain Management — $2.9B in cash plus all of Grain's 600 MHz licences — with the low-band holdings now being marketed to utilities, critical-infrastructure operators, and regional players. Sweden's PTS opened a consultation on using 3.8 GHz for local 5G (five-year site-specific permits), and India's regulator proposed safeguards for 5G slicing sold to consumers: an early signal of how policymakers will treat slicing as it moves from lab into commercial tariffs.Also in the round-up: Ooredoo Kuwait deployed a Network Data Analytics Function in its 5G core for faster, more proactive decisions; Vodafone Portugal ran a dedicated 5G standalone slice for SIBS card transactions at the Paredes de Coura festival, where ring-fenced capacity kept tills running through peak crowds; Turkiye hit 44.5M 5G subscribers four months after launch; and Rakuten Mobile confirmed it will scale back roaming on KDDI's network from October as its own coverage fills in.
          
        
        
          Why read it The fastest way to catch up on the week's spectrum, private-5G, and slicing moves. The India slicing-safeguards item deserves a second read — it is the first concrete regulatory posture on consumer slicing we have seen.
        
      
      
      
        
          Help Net Security
          An AI tool found 84 flaws in 5G network software — 23 still have no fix
        
        
        
          5G coresecurity flawsAI agents
        
        
        
          Researchers at Nanyang Technological University pointed a three-agent AI pipeline (iFinder) at the software that runs 4G/5G cores and got back 84 previously unreported vulnerabilities: 83 confirmed, 81 with CVE numbers, 23 still unpatched. The worst is a session hijack — an attacker who reaches an internal core link reuses the ID of a forwarding rule already assigned to a real subscriber, flags it as higher priority, and the network starts delivering the victim's traffic to the attacker. It ran end-to-end against OpenAirInterface's open-source 5G core, and replayed successfully on two commercial 5GCs.A second entry route is even more unsettling: an ordinary phone with a valid SIM hiding network control messages inside the data tunnel that carries its own uplink traffic — that trick worked against five of the seven open-source cores examined. The pipeline is useful rather than magic: on 22 previously known bugs it caught 15, and roughly a quarter of its reports are false positives — but every finding was manually reviewed and shipped with a working PoC before disclosure.
          
          flowchart LR
  A["Agent 1 · Code scan<br/>find unchecked inputs"] --> B["Agent 2 · 3GPP cross-check<br/>is validation done earlier?"]
  B --> C["Agent 3 · Exploit builder<br/>write, run, iterate"]
  C --> D["Verified findings<br/>84 flaws · 81 CVEs"]

          
        
        
          Why read it Rare case of AI-driven security research producing real CVEs in production packet-core stacks. If you run or audit a 5GC, the list of unpatched findings — and the question of whether commercial cores inherited the same gaps from open-source ancestry — is the story.
        
      
      
      
        
          arXiv
          Scaling 5G-TSN Bridges: Operating Regimes, Scheduling, and Time Sync
        
        
        
          3GPP Release 16 lets a 5G system act as a transparent IEEE 802.1 TSN bridge, but how many TSN endpoints can one NR cell actually bridge before per-flow QoS degrades? This paper simulates closed-loop control, machine vision, bulk telemetry, and 802.1AS traffic over a four-bearer SDAP architecture, sweeping endpoints from 1 to 40, and identifies three operating regimes. Below saturation, schedulers perform similarly; near saturation, QoS-aware proportional fair scheduling cuts critical-flow P99 latency by up to two orders of magnitude; under overload, only QoS-PF keeps near-complete delivery for the highest-priority traffic.Two more results that will matter in real deployments: isolating 802.1AS/gPTM traffic on a dedicated high-priority radio bearer stabilizes clock-servo behaviour, though lower-priority endpoints still see elevated synchronisation delay under saturation. And the evaluated sub-6 GHz, 30 kHz SCS configuration has an effective latency floor of about 2.25 ms — meaning sub-3 ms TSN deadlines likely need radio-configuration changes such as configured grants or a higher numerology.
          
        
        
          Why read it Practical sizing numbers for 5G+TSN industrial deployments — the kind of per-cell capacity ceiling that decides whether a use case is feasible before you buy any hardware.
        
      
      
    
  



  
    Security
    
      
      
        
          Wiz Research
          Wiz Red Agent exploits Snowflake vuln missed by GitHub Copilot
        
        
        
          Wiz's autonomous AI security agent (Red Agent) found a critical script-injection hole in Snowflake's public GitHub repo: any GitHub user could execute arbitrary commands on a GitHub Actions runner by opening an issue with a specially crafted title. The vulnerability went live just five days before discovery — introduced by a PR co-authored by Copilot Autofix powered by AI, which replaced the repo's sanitized input pattern with direct template interpolation, and GitHub's AI-assisted security review marked the change all-clear.The exploitation read like a horror story for AI-assisted development: Red Agent's proof-of-concept exfiltrated a live Jira credential, and when its first payload hit a bash syntax error, the agent autonomously analyzed the error, rewrote the payload to close the shell block correctly, and succeeded. Snowflake patched the same day after June disclosure and confirmed via audit logs that Wiz was the sole actor. Today's blog update clarifies the awkward detail: Copilot was the co-author that checked the merged PR and signed off on it.
          
        
        
          Why read it The cleanest public case study yet of the AI-on-AI security loop: one AI introduces the bug, another AI finds and exploits it, and the human review gates in between both passed. Required reading for anyone shipping AI-assisted code review.
        
      
      
    
  



  
    AI & Models
    
      
      
        
          The Register
          Stripe acquires AI model gateway OpenRouter for $7 billion
        
        
        
          OpenRouterAI gatewayM&A
        
        
        
          Stripe has agreed to acquire OpenRouter — the model gateway that gives developers one API into 400+ LLMs — for more than $7 billion, per Bloomberg. That is roughly five times the $1.3 billion valuation OpenRouter carried in a funding round just months earlier. The number that lands is the multiple: model routing and metering is being priced like a tollbooth, not a library.The strategic logic is payments, not models. OpenRouter sits between applications and model providers, so it already knows who calls which model, how much, and at what price. Fold that into Stripe's usage-based billing and agentic-payments push and you get the full stack: an agent picks a model, routes the request, and settles the bill — with one company holding the ledger.
          
          flowchart LR
  App[Your App] --> OR[OpenRouter<br/>400+ models]
  OR --> M1[Model A]
  OR --> M2[Model B]
  OR --> M3[Model C]
  OR --> SP[Stripe billing<br/>ledger + routing]

          
        
        
          Why read it A marker for where AI infrastructure money is consolidating. If you build on multi-model APIs, the routing layer's owner is now also the billing layer's owner — worth factoring into where you send traffic and what data flows through it.
        
      
      
      
        
          Artificial Analysis
          Qwen3.8 27B scores 52 on Artificial Analysis
        
        
        
          The open-weights Qwen 3.8 27B just posted a 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — well above the median for comparable models and, by the community's own benchmarks, neck and neck with DeepSeek V4 and GPT-5.6 Luna Max. It takes text and image input, carries a 256k-token context window, and costs nothing in licensing since the weights are open.The local-inference community has already put it through its paces: tuned llama.cpp configs are running it at 73k context on 16GB VRAM for agentic coding, with long-form reviews describing Sonnet-level performance plus a tendency to overthink that occasionally pushes toward frontier results. For a 27B-class open model, that is a large jump over the previous generation.
          
        
        
          Why read it The open-weights leaderboard sets the price/performance curve for local and edge inference. If you benchmark or deploy local models, this is the one to pull this week.
        
      
      
      
        
          Roboflow
          GPT 5.6 Sol is the best vision model OpenAI ever released
        
        
        
          OpenAI's GPT-5.6 lineup (Sol, Terra, Luna) launched with a heavy focus on computer use — UI agents, desktop control, 3D visualization — and Roboflow's VLM benchmark shows Sol is the strongest vision model OpenAI has shipped. The jump is sharpest in object detection: mAP@50 went from 13.8 (GPT-5.5) to 46.2 (Sol), and counting rose from 64.9% to 73.0%. Document layout detection — titles, tables, signatures — is a standout strength.Two practical caveats from the post that will save you real points: Sol degrades on images around 2000×2000 px or larger, especially at low reasoning effort (OpenAI confirmed this), so resize or crop before the API call. And coordinate format matters — absolute XYXY in image pixels is the winning prompt for GPT-5.6; using the wrong convention cost roughly 15 mAP points in their runs.
          
        
        
          Why read it If you build on VLMs for detection, OCR, or data extraction, the resolution and coordinate-format details are the difference between a demo and a production pipeline.
        
      
      
      
        
          GitHub
          llama.cpp v0.1.0 — the first semantic version
        
        
        
          llama.cpp has dropped its sequential build numbers (b10456 and friends) and adopted semantic versioning — v0.1.0 is the first semver tag, cut this week. A small ceremony, but it signals the project has settled into a stable release cadence after years of build-number churn.For anyone running local inference stacks, this is the version to start pinning against. The GGML quantization formats are the substrate of the entire local/edge inference ecosystem — the same formats that make 27B-class models like this week's Qwen 3.8 run on 16GB VRAM and consumer hardware.
          
        
        
          Why read it A one-minute item, but the versioning change is worth knowing before you pin dependencies in any local inference pipeline.
        
      
      
    
  



  
    Research & World Models
    
      
      
        
          arXiv
          Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin
        
        
        
          digital twintest-time
        
        
        
          A frontier coding agent writes an executable world model of an unknown game (ARC-AGI-3 style) from simulation and interaction alone — no hand-engineered model per task. The harness enforces replay validation: the agent is not allowed to act until its program reproduces every previously observed transition, and each mismatch between prediction and reality becomes a counterexample used to repair the model. Result: 179 of 183 levels cleared (97.8%), more action-efficient than humans on 88.3% of those levels, and the goal inferred before any reward signal on 87.2%.The ablation is the punchline. Played directly, the base model scores 7.8%. An off-the-shelf harness lifts it to 61.1%. The twin world model lifts the same base model to 93.3%. The authors' conclusion: building a usable world model is simpler than anticipated — the harder problem is inferring the right goal.
          
          flowchart LR
  O["Observe transitions"] --> P["World model<br/>predicts next state"]
  P --> M{"Match?"}
  M -- "no" --> R["Mismatch = counterexample<br/>repair the model"]
  R --> P
  M -- "yes" --> A["Act in the real game"]
  A --> O

          
        
        
          Why read it The cleanest current statement of a digital twin as an inference substrate: build the twin, replay against it, repair on mismatch, act only when the twin is faithful. The pattern transfers almost literally to network state estimation.
        
      
      
      
        
          arXiv
          Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance
        
        
        
          world modelsnext-state
        
        
        
          Interactive game world models typically generate pixels autoregressively, forcing structured properties — pose, geometry, occlusion — to be maintained implicitly by the generative sequence, which drifts over long horizons. Marionette inverts this: a two-stage autoregressive dynamics model predicts an explicit, interpretable 276-dimensional 3D world state (multi-entity articulated skeletons, metric root trajectories, rotations); a zero-parameter graphics bridge converts that state into pose-control video by computing geometry and occlusion in closed form; and a control-conditioned video-diffusion model synthesizes photorealistic RGB from the structured controls.The key property is that the state is directly controllable and repairable. Left free, two generated characters drift 21.2 m apart with a third of frames showing ground penetration; imposing two simple rules on the explicit state — a terrain collider and a separation cap — cuts penetration by 66% with no change to the observation model. Routing appearance through the predicted state costs no detectable fidelity: FVD of 831 versus 799 for recorded pose.
          
        
        
          Why read it A strong argument for explicit state in world models — the predict-state, render-appearance split that digital-twin work has argued for years, now demonstrated at game scale with numbers.
